html:
Diego Maradona was an Argentine footballer, one of the greatest of all time. He captained Argentina to victory in the 1986 World Cup in Mexico.

He grew up in a shanty town on the edge of Buenos Aires and played for Boca Juniors, Barcelona and Napoli, which he led to its first Italian titles. In the quarter-final of 1986 against England, four years after the Falklands War, he scored twice: first with his hand, which he called the hand of God, then after dribbling past half the English team, a goal often called the best ever.

His later life was troubled by cocaine addiction and a ban for doping at the 1994 World Cup. He died in 2020, and millions mourned him in Argentina, where he is close to a saint, much like football heroes such as Pelé in Brazil.
sum: Diego Maradona was an Argentine footballer, one of the greatest of all time. He captained Argentina to victory in the 1986 World Cup in Mexico.
